title: Admin - Track Admin Assignment Details - Accessibility Test Plan (WCAG 2.1 AA)
overview: Accessibility testing of the Admin User Role Management - Track Admin Assignment Details feature on the Y4J platform. This feature displays 'Assigned date' and 'Assigned by' information on each admin card for accountability tracking. The data is immutable and stored in audit logs. Edge cases include missing assignment records and legacy admin accounts without assignment metadata. Covers WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for semantic structure, screen reader compatibility, visual requirements, and handling of missing data states.

testCases.title: Assigned date field has programmatic label-value association
testCases.componentElement: Assigned date label and value on admin card
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, Internal Administrators page is loaded with at least one admin card that has assignment details
steps: Navigate to an admin card using screen reader
Locate the 'Assigned date' information
Verify the label 'Assigned date' (or similar) is programmatically associated with its value
Verify screen reader announces both the label and the date value together
expectedResults: Screen reader announces the label-value pair (e.g., 'Assigned date: January 15, 2026')
Label and value are programmatically associated (via dt/dd, aria-label, or label element)
The date value is not announced without its label context
Information is not conveyed solely through visual positioning
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users understand the assigned date for each admin

testCases.title: Assigned by field has programmatic label-value association
testCases.componentElement: Assigned by label and value on admin card
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with assignment details is displayed
steps: Navigate to an admin card using screen reader
Locate the 'Assigned by' information
Verify the label 'Assigned by' (or similar) is programmatically associated with its value
Verify screen reader announces both the label and the assigner's name together
expectedResults: Screen reader announces the label-value pair (e.g., 'Assigned by: Jane Smith')
Label and value are programmatically associated
The assigner name is not announced without its label context
Information is not conveyed solely through visual positioning
testCases.postconditions: Screen reader users understand who assigned each admin

testCases.title: Assignment details use semantic markup (definition list or structured data)
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with assignment details is displayed
steps: Inspect the assignment details section using developer tools
Verify label-value pairs use semantic markup (e.g., <dl>/<dt>/<dd>, <table>, or aria attributes)
Verify the structure conveys the relationship between labels and values programmatically
Navigate with screen reader to confirm relationships are announced
expectedResults: Assignment details use semantic markup (definition list, table, or ARIA-labeled structure)
Label-value relationships are programmatically determinable
Screen reader correctly pairs labels with their values
Structure is not relying solely on visual layout for meaning
testCases.postconditions: Assignment data structure is semantically correct

testCases.title: Date format is accessible and unambiguous
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with assigned date is displayed
steps: Read the assigned date value on the admin card
Verify the date format is unambiguous (e.g., 'January 15, 2026' or '15 Jan 2026', not '01/02/26')
Verify screen reader reads the date in a natural, understandable way
If a <time> element is used, verify the datetime attribute has a machine-readable format
expectedResults: Date is displayed in an unambiguous format (month name or clear day/month/year order)
Screen reader reads the date naturally (not as individual numbers)
If <time> element is used, datetime attribute provides ISO format for machines
Date is understandable regardless of locale assumptions
testCases.postconditions: Date is clearly understandable by all users

testCases.title: Assignment details text has sufficient color contrast
testCases.componentElement: Assigned date and Assigned by text
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with assignment details is displayed
steps: Use a contrast checker tool
Measure contrast of 'Assigned date' label text against card background
Measure contrast of the date value text against card background
Measure contrast of 'Assigned by' label text against card background
Measure contrast of the assigner name text against card background
expectedResults: All label text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against background
All value text has at least 4.5:1 contrast ratio against background
If labels use a lighter/secondary color, they still meet 4.5:1 minimum
Text is readable for users with low vision
testCases.postconditions: All assignment detail text is visually accessible

testCases.title: Assignment details are in logical reading order within admin card
testCases.componentElement: Assignment details position in card reading order
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card is displayed
steps: Navigate through the admin card content using screen reader
Document the reading order of all card elements
Verify assignment details appear in a logical position (after admin identity info)
Disable CSS and verify the DOM order matches the visual order
expectedResults: Reading order follows: Admin name → Email → Role → Status → Assigned date → Assigned by → Permissions
Assignment details are logically grouped together
DOM order matches visual presentation order
No confusing jumps in reading sequence
testCases.postconditions: Assignment details are in a meaningful position within the card

testCases.title: Missing assignment record is communicated accessibly
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, an admin card exists with missing assignment record
steps: Navigate to an admin card that has a missing assignment record
Verify a placeholder or message is displayed (e.g., 'Not available', 'N/A', or 'Unknown')
Verify screen reader announces the placeholder with its label context
Verify the placeholder is not an empty space or hidden element
expectedResults: Missing data shows a meaningful placeholder (e.g., 'Assigned date: Not available')
Screen reader announces the label and placeholder together
Placeholder text has sufficient contrast (4.5:1)
No empty or confusing gaps exist in the card content
Users understand that the data is unavailable (not just missing from the UI)
testCases.postconditions: Missing assignment data is clearly communicated

testCases.title: Legacy admin accounts without metadata display accessible fallback
testCases.componentElement: Legacy admin card without assignment metadata
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, a legacy admin account exists without assignment metadata
steps: Navigate to a legacy admin card that lacks assignment metadata
Verify the card handles the absence gracefully (shows placeholder or omits section with explanation)
Verify screen reader does not encounter broken or empty elements
Verify the card structure remains consistent with other admin cards
expectedResults: Legacy admin card shows appropriate fallback (e.g., 'Assigned date: Legacy account' or 'Assignment details unavailable')
Screen reader encounters no empty unlabeled elements
Card structure is consistent (same fields present, with fallback values)
Users understand this is a legacy account without tracking data
testCases.postconditions: Legacy accounts are handled gracefully without accessibility issues

testCases.title: Assignment details are readable at 200% browser zoom
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with assignment details is displayed
steps: Set browser zoom to 200%
Verify 'Assigned date' label and value are fully visible
Verify 'Assigned by' label and value are fully visible
Verify text does not overlap or get clipped
Verify the card layout adapts appropriately
expectedResults: All assignment detail text is fully readable at 200% zoom
No text is clipped, hidden, or overlapping
Labels and values remain visually associated
Card layout adapts (may stack vertically) without losing information
testCases.postconditions: Assignment details are fully readable at 200% zoom

testCases.title: Assignment details reflow at 320px viewport width
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with assignment details is displayed
steps: Resize browser viewport to 320px width
Verify assignment details are visible without horizontal scrolling
Verify labels and values remain associated visually
Verify no text is truncated or hidden
expectedResults: Assignment details reflow to fit narrow viewport
No horizontal scrollbar required
Labels and values remain clearly associated
All text is fully readable
testCases.postconditions: Assignment details work on narrow viewports

testCases.title: Assignment details text spacing can be overridden
testCases.componentElement: Assignment details with custom text spacing
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with assignment details is displayed
steps: Apply WCAG text spacing overrides (line-height 1.5x, paragraph spacing 2x, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em)
Verify assignment detail text remains readable
Verify no text is clipped or hidden by fixed-height containers
Verify labels and values do not overlap
expectedResults: Text remains readable with increased spacing
No text is clipped by fixed-height containers
Labels and values do not overlap
Layout adapts gracefully
testCases.postconditions: Assignment details support custom text spacing

testCases.title: Assignment details do not rely on color alone
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Super Admin, admin card with assignment details is displayed
steps: Observe the assignment details section
Check if any information is conveyed through color alone (e.g., colored text for different assigners)
View in grayscale mode
Verify all information is still understandable without color
expectedResults: No information is conveyed through color alone
In grayscale mode, all assignment details are still fully understandable
Labels and values are identifiable by text content, not color coding
If icons are used, they have text alternatives
testCases.postconditions: Assignment information is accessible regardless of color perception
